## 1. New LLM Versions / Major AI Lab Tools
**Date:** 2026-05-01  
**Source:** [OpenAI models, Codex, and Managed Agents come to AWS](https://openai.com/index/openai-on-aws/)  
**Summary:** OpenAI announced availability of its models, including GPT-5.5, on Amazon Bedrock, alongside Codex and Managed Agents for enterprise AWS users.  
**Why it matters:** This expands OpenAI distribution into a major enterprise cloud channel and reduces procurement friction for AWS-native customers.

**Date:** 2026-05-01  
**Source:** [OpenAI available at FedRAMP Moderate](https://openai.com/index/openai-available-at-fedramp-moderate/)  
**Summary:** OpenAI said U.S. government agencies can access its models in a FedRAMP Moderate environment, with Codex Cloud support planned through FedRAMP ChatGPT Enterprise workspaces.  
**Why it matters:** This is a public-sector access milestone, not just a product update; it opens a clearer path for regulated federal AI deployments.

## 5. Regulation & Policy

**Source:** [Academy rules approved for the 99th Oscars](https://press.oscars.org/news/awards-rules-and-campaign-promotional-regulations-approved-99th-oscarsr)

**Summary:** The episode argued that AI’s near-term constraint is token supply, with compute bottlenecks shaping business models. It cited GPU rental-price pressure, cloud demand for Trainium, and OpenAI commentary about compute as a limiting factor.
